headers.description: Optional headers to send with the request as a dictionary of header values.

Content-Type.description: The media type of the resource being requested, typically 'application/json'.

Authorization.description: The credentials to authenticate a user agent with a server, typically formatted as 'Bearer {token}'.

timeout.description: The maximum amount of time to wait for a response from the server, in seconds. A longer timeout may be necessary for slower network connections or overloaded servers. This is a float type value.

params.description: URL parameters to append to the URL. Sent as a dictionary of key-value pairs.

query.description: The query parameter for search or filtering.

page.description: The page number parameter for pagination. Used to retrieve a specific page of results.

auth.description: HTTP authentication credentials formatted as a tuple of strings (username, password).

cert.description: Path to the SSL client certificate file (.pem), if required for the request.

cookies.description: Cookies to send with the request as a dictionary of cookie names and values.

sessionid.description: Session identifier cookie, used to recognize client sessions on the server.

csrftoken.description: CSRF protection token cookie, used to prevent cross-site request forgery attacks.

proxies.description: Proxy settings as a dictionary, mapping protocol or protocol and hostname to the URL of the proxy.

http.description: Proxy URL to use for HTTP requests, including the port number.

https.description: Proxy URL to use for HTTPS requests, including the port number.

stream.description: Whether to stream the download of the response. If False, the response content will be immediately downloaded. Streaming is useful for handling large files or responses.

verify.description: Whether to verify the server's TLS certificate or not. Set to False to skip certificate verification, which is not recommended unless you are sure of the server's identity.

message.content:
Here’s a quick rundown of some popular cinemas near Times Square that usually offer films under two hours, along with tips on how to pick one that fits your schedule:

| Theater | Address | Typical Walking Distance | How to Check Showtimes |
|---------|---------|--------------------------|------------------------|
| **AMC Empire 25** | 234 W 42nd St, New York, NY 10036 | ~0.3 mi (≈10‑12 min walk) | Visit [AMC.com](https://www.amc.com/) → “Find a Movie” → enter ZIP 10036 → filter by “Showtime” & “Duration < 120 min”. |
| **Regal Broadway 14** | 225 W 43rd St, New York, NY 10036 | ~0.4 mi (≈12‑15 min walk) | Go to [Regal.com](https://regmovies.com/) → “Browse Movies” → choose “Near Me” → set max duration filter. |
| **Alamo Drafthouse Cinema – Brooklyn** | 200 Flatbush Ave, Brooklyn, NY 11201 | ~7 mi (not a walk; consider subway) | Check their site or app for “Shorts” & “Feature Length < 120 min”. |
| **Theater at Bryant Park** | 420 Lexington Ave, New York, NY 10170 | ~0.8 mi (≈15‑20 min walk) | Look up “Bryant Park Theatre” online; they often host indie shorts & feature films. |

### Quick Tips for Finding a 90–110 minute Film

1. **Use the “Duration” Filter**  
   Most theater chains let you filter by runtime. On AMC’s site, after selecting a location, click the “Filters” icon and tick “Under 2 Hours”.

2. **Check Indie & Short‑Film Programs**  
   Some venues (e.g., Alamo Drafthouse, Bryant Park Theatre) showcase short‑film festivals where many titles run < 30 min. Pair a short with a feature to stay under 2 hrs total.

3. **Look for “Premieres” or “Special Screenings”**  
   These events sometimes highlight newer releases that haven’t yet hit mainstream multiplexes but still fit the runtime window.

4. **Consider Suburban Options**  
   If you’re willing to take a quick subway ride, places like **AMC Lincoln Square 13** (West Village) or **Regal Union Square** (Union Square) offer a wider selection of indie titles that often run shorter.

---

#### Sample Search Example (AMC)

```text
URL: https://api.amctheatres.com/v3/movies?location=NYC&duration_lt=120
```

*(If you’d like me to pull real‑time showtimes for a particular date, just tell me the date and I’ll fetch the latest listings.)*

Let me know if you’d like me to look up today’s showtimes for a specific theater or help you book tickets!
